title: Element table
headers: heading (gameplay, shape, value, colour, timing, composition, camera)

rows.effect on feeling: Legibility supports confidence; wrong meaning creates frustration.
rows.mechanism: Communicate identity, consequence and magnitude; consistency lets players learn.

rows.numbers or ranges: 1–10 per caster/enemy/ally in Beardilocks’s reported League exercise; exact scale singly sourced. No numerical mapping to render parameters found.
rows.mechanism: Rank damage, control, dodgeability and decision relevance.
Primary border/time cue must represent the actionable area and state, regardless of ornamental halo.
League-specific conventions: green/soft heal, vertical knockup, floor ring/cylinder root. A stun is not automatically a knockup.
Show information to people who can act on it; preserve enemy-facing identity.

rows.numbers or ranges: VALORANT example: ≥1 rendered frame to muzzle/tracer; 40 ms one-way→80 ms round-trip plus processing.
rows.mechanism: Client feedback and authoritative outcome can occur at different times. Distinguish their meanings.

rows.effect on feeling: Softness/safety is a plausible starting hypothesis.
rows.effect on energy: Usually calmer when motion is also smooth.
rows.mechanism: Smooth contour scenes received safer judgements; a circle’s exact gameplay meaning remains learned.
Contour combinations affect threat judgments; no universal triangle-to-danger mapping proved.

rows.effect on feeling: Stable, constructed or mechanical by convention.
rows.effect on energy: Controlled or abrupt, depending on timing.
rows.mechanism: Inference: select rectilinear assets for the game’s established mechanical vocabulary; test interpretation.

rows.effect on feeling: Magic, gathering or vortex by convention.
rows.mechanism: Inference: inward flow can forecast a center; outward flow can show release. A decorative spiral is not a validated emotion trigger.

rows.effect on energy: Sharp transitions can read as forceful.
rows.mechanism: Distinct silhouette supports identification; soft secondary material should not replace the hit boundary.

rows.effect on energy: A clear shape can feel strong without more particles.
rows.mechanism: Choose a flipbook whose silhouette survives scale reduction and does not resemble another action.

rows.element: Line of action and directional blur
rows.numbers or ranges: no number found; inspect a paused frame.
rows.mechanism: A projectile tail should indicate travel direction; orient trails and stretched parts along the actual path.

rows.element: Arcs and radial versus directional release
rows.effect on energy: Spread conveys release; aimed motion conveys intent.
rows.mechanism: Arcs support secondary movement. Pick radial sheets for outward events, streaks/beams for directed events.

rows.effect on feeling: Organic richness; excessive detail can read as noise.
rows.effect on energy: Fine random change may add apparent agitation.
rows.mechanism: Reduce superfluous fine texture before increasing brightness; select coarser variants for small projections.

rows.effect on feeling: Weight, flexibility or punch, depending on sequence.
rows.numbers or ranges: no number found for a general character-size ratio.
rows.mechanism: Inference: tune visual scale separately from collision size; use squash/stretch for art without falsifying borders.

rows.effect on energy: Strong local contrast can elevate a peak.
rows.mechanism: Contrast is relational: inspect the effect against the actual background and competitors.

rows.effect on feeling: Room for special peaks and UI.
rows.numbers or ranges: 0% and 100% discouraged in LoL; no numeric middle-band limits found.
rows.mechanism: A title-specific allocation of value, not a physical law. Sparkball uses bolder values where restraint failed.
Make the important region distinct; broad uniform white removes internal structure.
Inference: asset glow affects the image; actual world lights and post bloom are separate layers with separate costs. Check readability without optional polish.

rows.effect on energy: A coordinated light pulse can reinforce a peak.
rows.mechanism: Inference: place a brief world-light response at the same spatial event; avoid large uniform wash that erases silhouettes.

rows.numbers or ranges: One dominant hue role; no percentage split found.
rows.mechanism: Complementary hues need hierarchy; palette width is a design choice.

rows.numbers or ranges: no number found for a universal saturation range.
rows.mechanism: High saturation is useful only relative to context; brightest/most saturated does not guarantee gaze.

rows.effect on energy: Peak at core or actionable edge as needed.
rows.mechanism: Inference: recolour layers by function; do not insist every effect has a white center when the border is the gameplay message.
Inference: hot-core→warm flame→dark smoke is a material/story cue, not a universal recipe; choose library states and tint curves accordingly.

rows.element: Hue meaning, team and danger colours
rows.numbers or ranges: 4598 participants; 30 nations; 22 languages; r=.88 association-pattern similarity.
rows.mechanism: Study measured colour terms and emotion associations, not emotions induced by VFX. Keep team identity consistent and redundant with shape.

rows.numbers or ranges: no number found for general windup milliseconds.
rows.mechanism: Communicate impending gameplay when a reaction window exists; cosmetic windup must not delay responsive controls.

rows.numbers or ranges: no number found for general punch frames.
rows.mechanism: A strong state change contrasts with preparation; align the visible consequence with the authored gameplay event.
Coordinate changes in shape, motion, value and sound rather than raising every parameter equally.

rows.effect on energy: Falls from peak; can preserve local activity.
rows.mechanism: Different parts settle at different times; secondary action supports the main event.
Retire the active signal when gameplay ends; residual art can lose opacity/value/size without suggesting continued danger.
Retiming can change interpretation; use curves and holds to serve the event, not because every parameter must ease.

rows.effect on feeling: Brief readable action with an outro.
rows.numbers or ranges: Main action finished or dissipating by first 25% of lifetime, reported for Sparkball.
rows.mechanism: A named title-specific practice. Do not copy onto charges, sustained hazards or other games as a requirement.
rows.evidence level: industry practice: firsthand Sparkball observation; no independent validation; not a universal default

rows.effect on feeling: Designed erosion can feel less like a card vanishing.
rows.mechanism: Inference: prefer a suitable premade breakup sequence when available; fade is not inherently wrong, and state expiry may need a crisp end.
Inference: separate cosmetic residue from active-damage cues; preserve enemy, pickup and path visibility.

rows.effect on energy: Cadence is distinct from event duration.
rows.numbers or ranges: Arithmetic: frame duration=1000/fps ms; on 2s at 24 fps=83.33 ms per drawing, not a universal 12 fps game setting.
rows.mechanism: Inference: preserve cadence while timing the hit marker independently; display, simulation and flipbook rates are different.

rows.effect on energy: One meaningful emphasis within the event.
rows.numbers or ranges: no number found for optimal emitter/layer count.
rows.mechanism: Roles are not a mandate for three emitters. Name what each component contributes before adding it.

rows.effect on feeling: Ease of reading; a place for the eye to settle.
rows.effect on energy: Contrast between active and quiet regions.
rows.mechanism: The gameplay-bearing feature owns emphasis; decorative motion should not compete equally.

rows.effect on feeling: Sparse can feel delicate; dense can feel substantial or muddy.
rows.effect on energy: Density is not equivalent to impact.
rows.numbers or ranges: no number found for a universal particle cap.
rows.mechanism: Inference: compare clustered and uniform emission at equal cost; inspect whether empty spaces preserve semantic boundaries.

rows.effect on feeling: Confusion when nearby elements become difficult to distinguish.
rows.effect on energy: More activity may reduce usable information.
rows.numbers or ranges: n=50; 82%/94% model variance explained, not a screen budget.
rows.mechanism: Spacing and eccentricity affect identification; tests used letters, not combat particles.

rows.effect on feeling: Attention can follow meaning instead of brightness.
rows.effect on energy: High saliency need not mean high usefulness.
rows.numbers or ranges: Model≈20 Hz selection; not an effect timing recommendation.
rows.mechanism: Goals, history, reward, scene structure and bottom-up features jointly guide search.

rows.effect on feeling: Alerting or distraction, conditional on task.
rows.mechanism: An irrelevant rotation onset captured attention in one search mode and was avoided in another.

rows.numbers or ranges: ERP effects 140/280 ms; no usable VFX detection threshold found.
rows.mechanism: Looming interacted with emotion/distance; reaction-time main effect was nonsignificant.

rows.effect on feeling: Intended force or instability; may be annoying.
rows.numbers or ranges: Eiserloh model: trauma t in [0,1]; shake proportional to t² or t³. No universal amplitude, frequency or duration found.
rows.mechanism: Industry model: event accumulation and linear decay drive smoothed-noise motion. Use separate amplitude, frequency and recovery controls; comfort guidance favors optional reduction/off.
rows.source, tier and year: CAM01 A 2016 pre-2020; SA04 A 2022 living guidance

rows.numbers or ranges: Lin reports Guilty Gear Xrd light hit-stop 7 frames and heavy approximately 10 frames; reference fps unverified, so no ms conversion. These are observations, not defaults.
rows.mechanism: Lin reports title-specific examples, without validated frame-rate conversion. Inference: distinguish world, animation, camera and local-VFX pause; local visuals do not pause server damage.
Inference: align kick direction to action, preserve control and test recovery while tracking another target.

rows.effect on feeling: Intended focus, speed or scale emphasis.
rows.mechanism: Lin describes cinematic camera focus/zoom examples. Inference: test projected hitbox readability throughout FOV changes; preserve a reduced-motion option.
Lin describes finishing-attack slow-motion examples. Inference: separate spectacle timing from player reaction and multiplayer simulation; a local effect rate is not global slow motion.

rows.numbers or ranges: no number found for an aesthetic default; safety criteria are in Output 3.
rows.mechanism: Inference: bind the flash to the actual moment; test the aggregate sequence, including overlapping effects, for safety.

rows.effect on feeling: Intended edge framing, injury or mood.
rows.mechanism: Inference: never make the obscured periphery carry the only usable hazard cue.
Inference: judge benefit against split-edge loss of precision; preserve a reduced-effects alternative.
Inference: distinguish a directional asset smear from full-screen blur; retain readable target and path detail.
Inference: acceptable only while all required gameplay information stays legible; gameplay depth does not follow a film camera automatically.

intro: The practitioner headings organize controllable visual choices. Feeling and energy descriptions express design intent unless a study directly measured them. No universal safe count, duration, brightness ratio or emotional mapping is implied.
